{{Quote|They'll take you out when you're not paying attention.|Jo Ewsli|<ref name="eas">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref>}}
'''Howlrunners''' were predatory creatures native to the [[Desert/Legends|deserts]] of the [[Wild Space]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kamar/Legends|Kamar]] who were renowned for their ferocity and dedication to the hunt. Known for their unsettling, [[Human/Legends|Human]] skull-like face, howlrunners were regarded as the most dangerous of Kamar's beasts, hunting in packs and chasing down prey with incredible stamina. Howlrunners were known throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] as uncommonly tenacious predators, although by the era of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] they had become endangered on Kamar, as they had become a popular target for big-game hunters. Their reputation was widespread enough that during the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Era]], the [[Incom Corporation/Legends|Incom Corporation]] named the [[I-7 Howlrunner]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] after the beast.

==Biology and appearance==
Omnivorous predators native to the desolate [[Desert/Legends|deserts]] of [[Kamar/Legends|Kamar]],<ref name="des">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> howlrunners were named after the loud howling sound they made while hunting their prey. [[Canine/Legends|Canine]] in appearance, howlrunners were distinguished by their heads, which had a resemblance to a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Bone/Legends|skull]] that many considered unnerving.<ref name="hsc" /> The "skull" was actually a layer of cartilage and bone covering the flesh underneath&mdash;scientists believed that it evolved to better allow howlrunners to burrow through the rocky ground of Kamar.<ref name="eas" /> The beasts averaged about 1.1 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length, and despite their relative lack of speed, were effective hunters due to their incredible stamina.<ref name="hsc" />

==Behavior==
{{Quote|I was on Kamar several years ago and witnessed a pack of howlrunners chasing down their prey. They ripped it apart, not necessarily because they outpowered their prey, but because they were quicker and more agile than their opponent. They took small nips out of the creature until it finally fell.|Jo Ewsli|<ref name="eas" />}}
Considered to be the most dangerous of all the beasts of Kamar, howlrunners hunted in packs, working cooperatively on their hunts to track and overtake much larger creatures. Howlrunner packs could reach great numbers, as they migrated together to find new hunting grounds and carve extensive dens out of the rocky terrain.<ref name="eas" /> Although they were native to the Kamar deserts, they could thrive in any habitat, and were known to travel great distances in search of prey. Howlrunners preferred to ambush their prey, lying in wait within the scrub plants of the [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]] before attacking and wounding passing animals. Once the chase was on, howlrunners were victorious because of their tireless persistence, making up for their lack of speed by simply chasing their targets until they collapsed.<ref name="hsc" /> They also used the characteristic howl that gave them their name to disorient their prey and make them easier to track.<ref name="eas" />

==History==
{{Quote|As I sat watching the howlrunners, the walls of the safari dome seemed to melt away. For a brief moment, I was part of the pack, hunting and howling with these magnificent predators. I have spent the rest of my life trying to recapture that feeling, from the cockpit of a starfighter.|Excerpt from ''[[The Anthropology of Engineering]]'' by Jo Ewsli|<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels">''[[The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref>}}
For many [[Standard year/Legends|years]], howlrunners were renowned for their tenacity and ferocity, with their reputation extending far beyond Kamar. In the waning days of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Sharad Hett]] earned the moniker "Howlrunner" due to his dedication and bravery.<ref name="jvs">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> Later, during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the [[Incom Corporation/Legends|Incom Corporation]] developed the [[I-7 Howlrunner]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] for the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], designing it in a way that the manufacturer felt reflected the fierceness of its namesake.<ref name="des" /> [[Engineer/Legends|Engineer]] [[Jo Ewsli]], inspired by a personal experience watching a pack of howlrunners on the hunt while on a trip to Kamar, directly chose the name "Howlrunner" in their honor. However, by the era of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], howlrunners had become an endangered [[Species/Legends|species]] on their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], owing to their popularity as big game&mdash;hunters traveled from far and wide to Kamar to hunt howlrunners for their famous skulls. Many howlrunners were also carried off to be placed into fighting rings, which were widely illegal across the New Republic.<ref name="eas" /> In addition, Howlrunners were hunted by the native [[Kamarian Badlander]]s, to whom boiled howlrunner was a valuable delicacy.<ref name="hsr">''[[Han Solo's Revenge]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The howlrunner was first mentioned in ''[[Han Solo's Revenge]]'', a novel written by [[Brian Daley]] and released in [[1979]].<ref name="hsr" /> It later received an entry in [[2001]]'s [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']], which provided extensive background information on the creature along with its first illustration, by [[R. K. Post]].<ref name="eas" />
